body: {"items":[{"id":"2026-23838","title":"Establishment of Class E Airspace; Columbus, TX","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/23/2026-23838/establishment-of-class-e-airspace-columbus-tx","summary":"This action proposes to establish Class E airspace at Columbus Community Hospital Heliport, Columbus, TX. The FAA is proposing this action to support new instrument procedures and instrument flight rule (IFR) operations.","publishedAt":"2026-11-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23836","title":"Amendment of Class E Airspace; Del Rio, TX","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/23/2026-23836/amendment-of-class-e-airspace-del-rio-tx","summary":"This action amends the Class E airspace at Del Rio, TX. This action is the result of a biennial review of the airspace associated with Laughlin Air Force Base (AFB), Del Rio, TX. This proposal also updates the name and geographic coordinates of Laughlin AFB to coincide with the FAA's aeronautical database. This action brings the airspace into compliance with FAA orders and supports instrument flight rule (IFR) procedures and operations.","publishedAt":"2026-11-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23824","title":"Amendment of Class D and E Airspace and Removal of Class E Airspace Over Lebanon, NH","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/23/2026-23824/amendment-of-class-d-and-e-airspace-and-removal-of-class-e-airspace-over-lebanon-nh","summary":"This action proposes to amend Class D and Class E airspace over Lebanon, NH. This action would increase the lateral dimensions of the Lebanon, NH, Class D airspace to appropriately contain Instrument Flight Rules (IFR) operations at the Lebanon Municipal Airport. This action would also update verbiage in the Class D airspace legal description to comply with current FAA guidance. This action would also update the geographic coordinates for the airport in both the Class D and Class E5 airspace legal descriptions. This action would also remove the exclusions for adjacent Class E5 airspace from the Lebanon, NH, Class E5 airspace legal description. This action would also remove the Lebanon, NH, Class E4 airspace, which is no longer necessary for IFR operations at the airport.","publishedAt":"2026-11-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23786","title":"Miscellaneous Technical Amendments; Technical Amendment","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/23/2026-23786/miscellaneous-technical-amendments-technical-amendment","summary":"This technical amendment contains non-substantive corrections to address typographical errors, editorial errors, and outdated or incorrect references in various parts of FAA regulations.","publishedAt":"2026-11-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23784","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities: Requests for Comments; Clearance of a Renewed Approval of Information Collection: Federal Aviation Regulation Part 119-Certification: Air Carriers and Commercial Operators","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/23/2026-23784/agency-information-collection-activities-requests-for-comments-clearance-of-a-renewed-approval-of","summary":"In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, FAA invites public comments about our intention to request the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) approval to renew an information collection. The Federal Register Notice with a 60-day comment period soliciting comments on the following collection of information was published on September 11, 2026. The collection involves requirements necessary under parts 135, 121, and 125 to comply with Federal Aviation Regulation part 119--Certification: Air Carriers and Commercial Operators. The FAA will use the information it collects and reviews to ensure compliance and adherence to regulations and, if necessary, to take enforcement action on violators of the regulations.","publishedAt":"2026-11-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23774","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities: Notice of Request for an Extension of a Currently Approved Information Collection","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/23/2026-23774/agency-information-collection-activities-notice-of-request-for-an-extension-of-a-currently-approved","summary":"The FHWA invites public comments about our intention to request the Office of Management and Budget's (OMB) approval for extension of an existing information collection that is summarized below under SUPPLEMENTARY INFORMATION. We are required to publish this notice in the Federal Register by the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995.","publishedAt":"2026-11-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23770","title":"Request for Comments on the Renewal of a Previously Approved Information Collection: Information To Determine Seamen's Reemployment Rights-National Emergency","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/23/2026-23770/request-for-comments-on-the-renewal-of-a-previously-approved-information-collection-information-to","summary":"MARAD invites public comments on its intention to request Office of Management and Budget (OMB) approval to renew an information collection in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995. The proposed collection OMB 2133-0526 (Information to Determine Seamen's Reemployment Rights--National Emergency) is used to determine if U.S. civilian mariners are eligible for reemployment rights under the Maritime Security Act of 1996. MARAD is required to publish this notice in the Federal Register to obtain comments from the public and affected agencies.","publishedAt":"2026-11-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23769","title":"Request for Comments on the Renewal of a Previously Approved Information Collection: Application To Participate; Voluntary Tanker Agreement","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/23/2026-23769/request-for-comments-on-the-renewal-of-a-previously-approved-information-collection-application-to","summary":"MARAD invites public comments on its intention to request Office of Management and Budget (OMB) approval to renew an information collection in accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995. The proposed collection OMB 2133-0505 (Application to Participate; Voluntary Tanker Agreement) is used to determine capacity commitments by participants in the event the Agreement is activated to meet the essential need for the transportation of petroleum and petroleum products in bulk by sea. There are no changes since the last renewal. MARAD is required to publish this notice in the Federal Register to obtain comments from the public and affected agencies.","publishedAt":"2026-11-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23764","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities: Requests for Comments; Clearance of Renewed Approval of Information Collection: Domestic and International Flight Plans","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/23/2026-23764/agency-information-collection-activities-requests-for-comments-clearance-of-renewed-approval-of","summary":"In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, FAA invites public comments about our intention to request the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) approval to renew an information collection. The Federal Register Notice with a 60-day comment period soliciting comments on the following collection of information was published on July 13, 2026, three comments were received. The collection involves extracting flight data such as aircraft, routing speed, etc. from domestic and international flights. FAA Form 7233-1 (Domestic) and FAA Form 7233-4 (International), Flight Plan: Both forms are used to collect Domestic flight plan information and used to govern the flight of aircraft for the protection and identification of aircraft and property and persons on the ground. The information is used by air traffic controllers, search and rescue (SAR) personnel, flight standards inspectors, accident investigators, military, law enforcement, and the Department of Homeland Security.","publishedAt":"2026-11-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23763","title":"Notice of Intent To Designate as Abandoned Heli-Support, Inc. Supplemental Type Certificates","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/23/2026-23763/notice-of-intent-to-designate-as-abandoned-heli-support-inc-supplemental-type-certificates","summary":"This notice announces the FAA's intent to designate Heli- Support, Inc. Supplemental Type Certificate (STC) Nos. SH5889NM, SR10117LA-D, SR00122LA-D, SH6024NM, SR00126LA-D, SH5474NM, SR00057DE, SH1500NM, SH8032NM, SH7054NM, SR00121LA-D, SH8046NM, SR00120LA-D, SR00127LA-D, SH6039NM, and SH8045NM as abandoned and make the related engineering data available upon request. The FAA has received a request to provide engineering data concerning these STCs. The FAA has been unsuccessful in contacting Heli-Support, Inc. concerning these STCs. This action is intended to enhance aviation safety.","publishedAt":"2026-11-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23752","title":"Airworthiness Directives; ATR-GIE Avions de Transport Régional Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/23/2026-23752/airworthiness-directives-atr-gie-avions-de-transport-rgional-airplanes","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all ATR-GIE Avions de Transport R[eacute]gional Model ATR42 and ATR72 airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by a review of mooring loads that revealed that winds within the currently defined wind profiles could lead to loads exceeding the certification limits on the nose landing gear (NLG) and main landing gear (MLG) while the airplane is moored. This proposed AD would require revising the existing maintenance or inspection program, as applicable, to incorporate a revised maintenance procedure (MP) for mooring the airplane. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23749","title":"Airworthiness Directives; ATR-GIE Avions de Transport Régional Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/23/2026-23749/airworthiness-directives-atr-gie-avions-de-transport-rgional-airplanes","summary":"The FAA proposes to adopt a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all ATR-GIE Avions de Transport R[eacute]gional Model ATR42-500 and ATR72-212A airplanes. This proposed AD was prompted by reports of two in-service events during takeoff where an internal failure of the integrated air system control (IASC) software analog-to-digital converter generated erroneous pressure digital values, leading to uncommanded full-speed closure of the outflow valve and a high negative cabin altitude rate. This proposed AD would require installing improved IASC software. This proposed AD would also prohibit the installation of affected software under certain conditions. The FAA is proposing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23733","title":"Notice of Final Federal Agency Actions on Proposed Transportation Project in California","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/23/2026-23733/notice-of-final-federal-agency-actions-on-proposed-transportation-project-in-california","summary":"The FHWA, on behalf of the California Department of Transportation (Caltrans), is issuing this notice to announce actions taken by Caltrans that are final agency actions. This action consists of two related actions, the Gaviota Creek Improvement Project and the Gaviota Creek Permanent Restoration Project, that have been combined for Project Approval and Environmental Document (PA&ED) and future phases, including construction if feasible. This project consists of improvements to historical fish access at several locations within Gaviota Creek and adjacent to U.S. 101 in Santa Barbara County from postmile 46.9 to 47.3. The project includes the phased removal of six grade control structures, construction of fish passage elements, removal of an existing sacked concrete revetment wall, installation of a retaining wall to stabilize the highway embankment, and native species replanting.","publishedAt":"2026-11-23","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23716","title":"Agency Information Collection Activities; Renewal of an Approved Information Collection: Generic Clearance of Customer Satisfaction Surveys","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/20/2026-23716/agency-information-collection-activities-renewal-of-an-approved-information-collection-generic","summary":"In accordance with the Paperwork Reduction Act of 1995, FMCSA announces its plan to submit the Information Collection Request (ICR) described below to the Office of Management and Budget (OMB) for review and approval and invites public comment. Executive Order (E.O.) 12862 directs Federal agencies to provide service to the public that matches or exceeds the best service available in the private sector. These principles were reaffirmed in E.O. 13571. In order to work continuously to ensure that the Agency's programs are effective and meet our customers' needs, FMCSA requests approval to renew an ICR titled, \"Generic Clearance of Customer Satisfaction Surveys.\" This ICR allows FMCSA to continue collecting feedback on FMCSA's service delivery. By feedback the Agency means information that provides useful insights on perceptions and opinions but are not statistical surveys that yield quantitative results that can be generalized to the population of study.","publishedAt":"2026-11-20","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23715","title":"Hours of Service (HOS) of Drivers; American Pyrotechnics Association (APA); Request To Include an Additional Member Company to Current APA HOS Exemptions","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/20/2026-23715/hours-of-service-hos-of-drivers-american-pyrotechnics-association-apa-request-to-include-an","summary":"FMCSA announces its decision to grant the American Pyrotechnics Association's (APA) application to add new member company North Star Fireworks LLC (North Star) to the APA's existing exemptions during the designated Independence Day periods. The exemptions allow drivers to exclude off-duty and sleeper berth time of any length from the calculation of the 14-hour limit and to use paper records of duty status (RODS) in lieu of electronic logging devices (ELDs). FMCSA has determined that the exemptions, subject to the terms and conditions set forth below, are likely to achieve a level of safety that is equivalent to, or greater than, the level of safety that would be achieved in the absence of the exemptions.","publishedAt":"2026-11-20","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23697","title":"Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/20/2026-23697/airworthiness-directives-the-boeing-company-airplanes","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for certain The Boeing Company Model 737-600, -700, -700C, -800, and -900 series airplanes. This AD was prompted by a review of the autothrottle (A/T) cruise thrust split monitor (MONFD) and the determination that there is a potential for latent loss of spoiler sensor position data or erroneous spoiler sensor position data. This AD requires repetitive aileron built-in test equipment (BITE) tests of the digital flight control system and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-20","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23691","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Airbus SAS Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/20/2026-23691/airworthiness-directives-airbus-sas-airplanes","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus SAS Model A330-841 and A330-941 airplanes. This AD was prompted by a report of cracks on the discharge outlet of certain engine fire extinguisher bottles. This AD requires modification of affected fire extinguisher bottles and prohibits the installation of affected parts. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-20","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23688","title":"Airworthiness Directives; The Boeing Company Airplanes","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/20/2026-23688/airworthiness-directives-the-boeing-company-airplanes","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all The Boeing Company Model 757 airplanes. This AD was prompted by reports of crack damage at existing reinforcing repairs in the fuselage frame lower lobe areas in certain sections. This AD requires doing an inspection for any existing reinforcing repairs in the fuselage frame lower lobe areas in certain sections and applicable on-condition actions. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-20","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23684","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/20/2026-23684/airworthiness-directives-airbus-helicopters","summary":"The FAA is superseding Airworthiness Directive (AD) 2025-13- 09, which applied to all Airbus Helicopters Model AS-365N2, AS 365 N3, EC 155B, EC155B1, SA-365N, and SA-365N1 helicopters. AD 2025-13-09 required inspecting the tightening torque, reporting the results of the inspections, and, depending on the results of the inspection, taking corrective action. Since the FAA issued AD 2025-13-09, the manufacturer determined that additional inspections of the main rotor (MR) servo-controls nut torque are required. This AD retains some of the actions of AD 2025-13-09 and requires additional inspections and, depending on the results of the inspection, corrective actions. This AD also requires reporting certain information to the manufacturer. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-20","source":"Federal Register"},{"id":"2026-23679","title":"Airworthiness Directives; Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Helicopters","url":"https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/11/20/2026-23679/airworthiness-directives-airbus-helicopters-deutschland-gmbh-ahd-helicopters","summary":"The FAA is adopting a new airworthiness directive (AD) for all Airbus Helicopters Deutschland GmbH (AHD) Model EC135P1, EC135P2, EC135P2+, EC135P3, EC135T1, EC135T2, EC135T2+, EC135T3, and EC635T2+ helicopters. This AD was prompted by a report of a separated tail rotor blade (TRB) assembly due to a crack caused by intergranular corrosion. This AD requires repetitively inspecting a certain TRB assembly for cracks and, depending on the results, removing any cracked TRB assembly from service and replacing an affected part as terminating action for the repetitive inspections. This AD also prohibits installing a certain TRB assembly on any helicopter unless certain requirements are met. The FAA is issuing this AD to address the unsafe condition on these products.","publishedAt":"2026-11-20","source":"Federal Register"}]}
